answer:
Focal loss multiplies binary cross-entropy by (1−p_t)^gamma and an optional class weight alpha_t. Easy examples receive less weight, while incorrect/confident examples retain a large loss. Computing log(p_t) from softplus avoids unstable log(sigmoid). gamma=0 recovers weighted BCE. alpha and gamma address different issues and should be tuned on a leakage-free validation set.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** $L=-\alpha_t(1-p_t)^\gamma\log p_t$ reduces easy-example contribution as $p_t\to1$. At $\gamma=0$ it becomes weighted BCE, a useful equivalence test. When differentiating, retain the gradient through the modulation term; treating it as a detached weight implements a different objective. [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.02002)

For the implementation or system context discussed above, see [1](https://amaarora.github.io/posts/2020-06-29-FocalLoss.html) and [2](https://gombru.github.io/2018/05/23/cross_entropy_loss/).
